# The model is not the agent

::: {.callout-note}
Draft brief, tier B. Bullets and references compiled from source discussions 01–08 (2026-11-16). `[LAB n]`, `[RESEARCH]`, `[PLAN]` and `[VERIFY]` mark what is still open. `vault:` paths point into the Obsidian vault.
:::

**Outcome (draft, #1):** keep a fleet working when a provider runs out of quota or goes down, within a token budget, with no lock-in. Check: kill a provider mid-run; the work completes on another, and spend stays under budget.

## The pattern
- "to build a workflow that requires a specific model to run is a sure sign that you're building the harness wrong… tight coupling leads to bad results" (02). The reader's test: can the workflow run on a different model?
- Model changes are "a design time decision", not a runtime one, made by a measure-and-improve loop that keeps running (04). Contrast the OpenAI guide's one-off "baseline on the top model, then swap down".
- Three layers, each changed at its own time: the workflow names a combo (design time), and a reviewed change sets the combo's members, outside runtime (04).
- Pick the model class for the step: putting a coding LLM on a reasoning step shows "you lack an understanding of what the step does… you might as well choose an image generator model" (01).
- Count accounts, not rungs. A fallback chain whose rungs share one credential fails as one unit (04, Claude, from the 2026-09-20 combo-guard measurement).
- Ceiling vs budget: a ceiling is a crude stop so one issue can't drain the day; a budget is sized to what the issue is worth (02). And even that is "oversimplifying": "time, token, compute, etc all must be considered", and "not all companies will value those costs the same way" (02).
- Budgets are counters in code that the model can see but not change. A plan may narrow a budget, never widen it (02, from the design).
- FinOps is a thread through the whole book, not just this chapter (02).
- Prefer open source, so you can contribute or fork. Build vs buy is decided by acceptance criteria: "why pay to reinvent that wheel?" (05)

## How I set it up
- 17+ providers plus local models, behind OmniRoute combos. `[VERIFY]` the count on the day.
- A per-run token ceiling, 200,000 by default (02, from the design). `[VERIFY]` it's still current.
- The replay set runs on local models, "so the costs are basically time and electricity" (02).

## How I decided, and what I gave up
- No per-issue budget yet: "setting a budget BEFORE we have a working product seems foolish at best, but it is something that should be built before we call our solution" complete (02).
- How to read Anthropic's finding that token spend explains most of performance: it comes from a search benchmark. In the fleet, spend and result came apart (02, Claude). The supporting numbers are held (see below).
